# `scan_iscope`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

UDP 4720 discovery request; the device answers with its discovery record (serial, name, model, activation, lock and client count).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / established (no persistent effect; 64-bit build) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, scan_iscope @0x1e7ae0 and UDP thread @0x1e6a80 (64-bit build; 32-bit builder @0x17b820); app 3.3.2 UDP scanner |

Sent as one CR- or LF-terminated JSON line in one UDP datagram to port 4720, normally to the Wi-Fi directed broadcast address (unicast is also processed). The handler is registered only on the UDP discovery socket, not on TCP 4700. Datagram boundaries are not line boundaries: the device keeps one line reader across datagrams and senders, ignores lines of four bytes or fewer, and replies to the source of the latest datagram, so a client should send the whole delimited request in one datagram. The reply is one datagram, unicast to the request's source address and port, with LF bytes removed and no line terminator appended. Unknown methods (code 103) get no reply, also inside batches. The device address is the reply's source address; the record has no address member.

Side effects: None persistent: reads identity, AP state, lock settings and licence files; starts read-only helper processes (boot-environment read, interface query); logs and sets a thread-local error code. Tier B because of the log writes and thread-local error state.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Matched exactly and case-sensitively. Fixed value `"scan_iscope"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | The app sends an empty string. The handler does not read params. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |
| 103 | Unknown method; the reply is suppressed on UDP, so nothing is sent | `method not found (silent)` |

No handler-level error branch is established.

## Example

Request, request - As sent by the app (CRLF follows on the wire):

```json
{"id":7,"method":"scan_iscope","params":""}
```

Reply, ok - Synthetic values; optional members vary by device:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scan_iscope","result":{"sn":"EXAMPLESN01","ssid":"S50_EXAMPLE","product_model":"Seestar S50","is_verified":true,"tcp_client_num":1,"connect_lock":false,"password":"md5-hex-placeholder","can_star_mode_sel_cam":false},"code":0,"id":7}
```
